Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from errors, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
 
Many people (A)/ have blamed the advent of technology (B)/ followed by globalization and digitization as one of the chief causes (C)/of continuous lose of jobs in the market /(D) No Error. /(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. the error lies in part D of the sentence. 
Key Points
Let us have a look at a few words mentioned in the sentence:
  • Lose is a verb.
  • Loss is a noun.
  • The word lose should be replaced by loss because the sentence needs a noun to be modified by the adjective continuous.
So the correct sentence is Many people have blamed the advent of technology followed by globalization and digitization as one of the chief causes of continuous loss of jobs in the market.
Additional Information
The Eight Parts of Speech:
  • A noun is the name of a person, place, thing, or idea.
    • Example: India, Rabbit, Cardamom, Lily, etc
  • A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun.
    • Example: I, me, he, she, herself, you, it, that, they, each, few, many, who, whoever, whose, someone, everybody, etc.
  • A verb expresses action or being.
    • Example: read, write, talk, walk, eat, drink, etc.
  • An adjective modifies or describes a noun or pronoun.
    • Example: small, large, square, round, poor, wealthy, slow, etc.
  • An adverb modifies or describes a verb, an adjective, or another adverb.
    • Example: quickly, loudly, softly, carelessly, etc.
  • A preposition is a word placed before a noun or pronoun to form a phrase modifying another word in the sentence.
    • Example: by, with, about, until, etc.
  • A conjunction joins words, phrases, or clauses.
    • Example: and, but, or, while, because, etc.
  • An interjection is a word used to express emotion.
    • Example: hurray, bravo, kudos, yay, wow, etc

The doctors looked at the report (A)/ and concluded that (B)/ the patient is (C) /now free of danger. (D)/ No Error. (E)/
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. the error lies in part D of the sentence. 
Key Points
Let us have a look at the meaning of few words given below:
  • The phrase 'free of' means 'clear of', 'untainted by', or 'simply without'.
  • In contrast, 'free from' suggests 'liberated from' or 'no longer oppressed by'.
  • Hence, free of should be replaced by free from.
  • Hence, the correct answer is 'D'.
So the correct sentence is: The doctors looked at the report and concluded that the patient is now free from danger.
Additional Information
Examples of 'free from' in a sentence are as follows:
  • Free from debt, she can now expand her business.
  • Allow us one day free from this nagging stuff.
  • A well-wisher needs advice free from criticism.

Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from errors, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
 
Rich should help poor /(A) as this is a really good way of /(B) removing the huge economic division /(C) which exists in a highly populated country like India. /(D) No Error. /(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A' i.e. the error lies in part A of the sentence. 
Key Points 
Let us look at few words given in the sentence
  • Rich and Poor represent the people.
  • Representations always use ‘the’.
  • Hence, rich and poor should be preceded by 'the'.
So the correct sentence is: The rich should help the poor as this is a really good way of removing the huge economic division which exists in a highly populated country like India.
Additional Information
Let us note the following about articles:
  • Articles are used before nouns or noun equivalents.
    • Example: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
    • Example: A man is known by the company he keeps.
  • Articles may be considered a type of adjective.
  • 'The' is used to indicate that the identity of the noun is known to the reader.
    • Example: The magician simply stole the show.
  • 'A, An' are used when the identity of the noun is not known.
    • Example: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

The teacher advised the students (A)/ to use water carefully (B)/ as much water are wasted (C)/ if used carelessly. (D)/ No Error. (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'C' i.e. the error lies in part C of the sentence. 
Key Points
Let us have a look at a few words given in the sentence:
  • The word much is used for uncountable nouns.
  • Hence, are should be replaced by the singular verb is.
So the correct sentence is: The teacher advised the students to use water carefully as much water is wasted if used carelessly.
Additional Information
Use of 'is' and 'are':
  • Both 'is' and 'are' are forms of the linking verb 'to be'.
  • Singular nouns use 'is'
  • Plural nouns use 'are'.
  • ​Examples:
    • Radha is excited about her first day of school. (Radha is singular)
    • The rabbits are playing in the backyard. (Rabbits is plural)
    • Maya’s desk is too tall for her. (Desk is singular)
    • The students are noisy in the morning. (Students is plural)

The Indian Space Research Organisation (A)/ has launch a series of satellites recently (B)/ thereby making India a potential hub (C)/ for scientific and technological research in near future. (D)/ No Error.(E)/
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. the error lies in part B of the sentence. 
Key Points
Let us have a look at the structure of the sentence:
  • The present perfect tense construction has + verb always takes the past participle form of the verb.
  • Hence, launch should be replaced with launched.
So the correct sentence is: The Indian Space Research Organisation has launched a series of satellites recently thereby making India a potential hub for scientific and technological research in the near future.
Additional Information

Main verbs have three basic forms:

  • the base form
    • ​e.g. talk, walk, drink, etc.
  • the past form
    • e.g. wrote, ate, slept, etc.
  • the -ed form
    • ​e.g. talked, walked, rocked, etc.
  • In a regular verb, the past participle is formed by adding "-ed". 
    • Example: talked, walked, rocked, etc

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 5. 

Key Points

  • To answer the question, refer to the first line of the fourth paragraph of the given passage -
  • The proposed mechanism for coin _______ would be a departure from the conventional machines which relied on banknotes for facilitating coin exchanges.
  • Above line talks about the mechanism of the QR-code based coin vending machine launched by RBI will will be different from the conventional machines which relied on banknotes for facilitating coin exchanges as it will be using UPI as the mode of payment for providing coins.

​Additional Information

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Accessibility'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

To answer the question let's first look at the meanings of the given word and all the words given in the options - 

  • Accessibility - fact of being able to be reached or obtained easily (अभिगम्यता)
    • For Example  - 
    • The new road is being built to increase accessibility to the town center.
  • Accountability - the fact of being responsible for what you do and able to give a satisfactory reason for it (जवाबदेही)
    • For Example - 
    • The end goal is to establish more accountability and improve teaching.
  • ​Conveyance - the process or system of transporting or taking somebody/something from one place to another (परिवहन)
    • For Example - 
    • Our company relies mainly on trains for the conveyance of goods to our customers.
  • Availability - the state of being available (उपलब्धता​)
    • For Example - 
    • Did you check the availability of this product online?
  • Liability - the state of being responsible for something (देयता)
    • For Example - 
    • They have denied any liability for the damage caused by the accident.
  • Immunity - the ability to avoid or not be affected by disease, criticism, punishment by law, etc. (प्रतिरक्षा)
    • For Example - 
    • Humans have developed immunity to this virus overtime.
  • ​After looking at the meanings of all the given words we can conclude that 'Availability' is the only word that is similar in meaning to the given word 'Accessibility'.​

​
Therefore, the correct answer would be 'Availability'.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Peculiar'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1.

Key Points

To answer the question let's first look at the meanings of the given word and all the words given in the options - 

  • Peculiar - unusual or strange (विचित्र)
    • For Example  - 
    • My parents looked at me with a very peculiar expression when I told them the news.
  • ​Uncanny - very strange; that you cannot easily explain (अस्वाभाविक/विचित्र​)
    • For Example - 
    • Some people say that dogs have an uncanny way of sensing bad people.
  • ​Sophisticated - having or showing a lot of experience of the world and social situations; knowing about fashion, culture, etc. (परिष्कृत​)
    • For Example - 
    • It's not easy to impress her, she is a highly sophisticated and elegant woman.
  • Naive - without enough experience of life and too ready to believe or trust other people (अनाड़ी​)
    • For Example - 
    • It's very naive of you to believe every word he says.
  • Untrustworthy - not able to be relied on as honest or truthful (बेईमान)
    • For Example - 
    • I thought that we could be good friends but he turned out to be quite untrustworthy.
  • Reliable - suitable or fit to be relied on (भरोसेमंद)
    • For Example - 
    • I want a reliable person to look after my business.
  • ​After looking at the meanings of all the given words we can conclude that 'Uncanny' is the only word that is similar in meaning to the given word 'Peculiar'.​

​
Therefore, the correct answer would be 'Uncanny'.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of the word 'Conventional'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

To answer the question let's first look at the meanings of the given word and all the words given in the options - 

  • Conventional - always behaving in a traditional or normal way (पारंपरिक)
    • For Example - 
    • Our boss is very conventional in her views.
  • Traditional - following or belonging to the customs or ways of behaving that have continued in a group of people or society for a long time without changing (परंपरागत)
    • For Example - 
    • The traditional way of life has almost disappeared from our societies.
    Extraordinary - very unusual and special (असाधारण)
    • For Example - 
    • She has extraordinary potential when it comes to Maths.
  • Temporary - lasting for a short time; not permanent (अस्थायी)
    • For Example - 
    • This medicine will give you temporary relief from the pain.
  • Enduring - continuing for a long time; lasting (स्थायी​)
    • For Example - 
    • Her most enduring qualities are her grace and elegance.
  • Disquieting - inducing feelings of anxiety or worry (बेचैन)
    • For Example - 
    • The news gave disquieting news of the earthquake.
  • After looking at the meanings of all the given words we can conclude that 'Extraordinary' is the only word that is opposite in meaning to the given word 'Conventional'.​

 

Therefore, the correct answer would be 'Extraordinary'.

questions.text: According to the passage, the vending machines would dispense coins against debit to the customer's account using which of the following payment methods?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

To answer this question refer to the the first line of the second paragraph of the given passage - 

  • 'In simple words, the vending machines would dispense coins with the requisite amount being debited from the customer’s account using United Payments Interface (UPI) instead of physical tendering of banknotes.'
  • After reading the above line we can conclude that the vending machines would dispense coins with the requisite amount being debited from the customer’s account using UPI instead of banknotes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4 i.e. UPI.

questions.text: As per the latest RBI bulletin, what was the total value of circulation of rupee coins as of December 30 last year?

questions.text: According to the passage, why the mandate to eliminate the physical tendering of banknotes was opted for the coin vending machine?

options.text: to promote the digital mode of payments
to achieve RBI's ultimate objective that is to operate the currency system of the country
to avoid fake currency being fed into the machines as it can not be checked right at that point of time

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

  • 'Further, the proposed machine would eliminate the need for physical tendering of banknotes and their authentication. It was observed that the currency being fed into the machines (for coin exchange) were often found to be fake and could not be checked right at that point of time. Thus, the mandate to eliminate the physical tendering of banknotes.'

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4 i.e. to avoid fake currency being fed into the machines as it can not be checked right at that point of time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank given in the passage.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Crucial.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "From day-to-day expenses to long-term budget forecasting, financial awareness is _______ for managing these factors'' is saying that financial awareness is necessary or very important for managing day-to-day expenses and long-term budget forecasting.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Crucial'.
  • Also, the use of the words ''awareness'' and ''managing'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'crucial' in the blank.
  • The word 'Crucial' means Extremely important.
    • Example: The early learning years are crucial to a child's educational development.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Complete Sentence: From day-to-day expenses to long-term budget forecasting, financial awareness is crucial for managing these factors.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • Peripheral means Of secondary or minor importance; not as important as the main aim, part, etc. of something.
    • Trivial means Of little importance; not worth considering.
    • Obscure means Not important or well-known.
    • Inconsequential means Not important, insignificant.

questions.text: Which of the following can be inferred from the third paragraph?

questions.text: According to the passage, financial illiteracy can lead to:

Managing and paying off debts, and understanding credit and investment products.
Poor credit, bankruptcy, housing foreclosure, and other negative consequences.

questions.text: Why financial awareness is important?

options.text: To understand and effectively use various financial skills.
To experience poorer employment opportunities and outcomes and lower income.
For not achieving seemingly unachievable goals.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '​To understand and effectively use various financial skills.'

  • From the above sentence, we can say that financial awareness is important to understand and effectively use various financial skills.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Imperative'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Vital.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Imperative' means Of vital importance; crucial.
    • Example: It is imperative that politicians should be good communicators.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Vital - Absolutely necessary; essential.
      • Example: A strong opposition is vital to a healthy democracy.
    • Superfluous - Unnecessary; not needed.
      • Example: She gave him a look that made words quite superfluous.
    • Insignificant - Too small or unimportant to be worth consideration.
      • Example: The Chief Inspector disliked being overburdened with insignificant detail.
    • Extraneous - Irrelevant or pointless.
      • Example: We shall ignore factors extraneous to the problem.
    • Dispensable - Not necessary; superfluous.
      • Example: Part-time workers are considered dispensable.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word 'Imperative' are "Vital, Essential, Necessary".
  • The antonyms of the word 'Imperative' are "Superfluous, Insignificant, Dispensable".

questions.text: Choose the antonym of the word 'Adequate'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Scant.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Adequate' means Satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity.
    • Example: The school lunch should be adequate to meet the nutritional needs of growing children.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Requisite - Necessary for a particular purpose.
      • Example: She lacks the requisite experience for the job.
    • Appropriate - Suitable or proper in the circumstances.
      • Example: The drug is not being produced in appropriate amounts.
    • Scant - Barely sufficient or inadequate.
      • Example: We have to ration the water because we only have a scant amount.
    • Ample - Enough or more than enough; plentiful.
      • Example: They had ample money for the trip.
    • Sufficient - Enough; adequate.
      • Example: There must be sufficient funds in your bank account to cover the check.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.text:
Select the phrase/connector from the given three options which can be used to form a single sentence from the two sentences given below, implying the same as expressed in the statement sentence.

The last glacial period ended more than 8,000 years ago. Its effects can still be felt today.

1. And its effects

2. Although the last

3. As well as the last glacial
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only 2.

Key Points

  • Let's use each phrase/connector given and analyse whether it can be used to properly form a single sentence or not:
    • And its effects: 
      • ​Single sentence: The last glacial period ended more than 8,000 years ago and its effects can still be felt today.
      • The conjunction 'and' is used either to connect either two similar sentences or to present two separate facts about a single thing
      • In this case, the time '800 years ago' and the time 'today'  are not similar and are not independent
      • Thus this is not a usable phrase/connector
    • Although the last:
      • Single sentence: Although the last glacial period ended more than 8,000 years ago, its effects can still be felt today.
      • The conjunction 'although' means 'inspite of the fact that' and is used to connect two contrasting sentences or phrases
      • In this case, the time '800 years ago' and the time 'today'  are contrasting phases of time
      • Thus this is a usable phrase/connector
    • As well as the last glacial:
      • Single sentence: As well as the last glacial period ended more than 8,000 years ago, its effects can still be felt today.
      • The connecting phrase 'as well as' implies the meaning 'and in addition'
      • It is always placed in between a noun/pronoun/verb/adjective pair and never at the beginning or the end of a sentence
      • Thus this is a grammatically incorrect construction
      • Also, even if we look at joining these sentences using the conjunction 'as well as' in the correct grammatical way, it would simply mean adding the two facts together without any relation which is not correct in this context (as was explained for the conjunction 'and')

 

The sentence after using the correct phrase/connector is: Although the last glacial period ended more than 8,000 years ago, its effects can still be felt today.

Additional Information

  • Conjunction: In grammar, conjunction is a part of speech that connects words, phrases, or clauses that are called the conjuncts of the conjunctions.
  • Meanings of the following words:
    • Effect: result or impact
    • Glacial: freezing or icy

questions.text: Train A is half the length of train B and moves at one-third of train B's speed. If train A takes 48 seconds to pass a man, how much time will it take for train B to pass train A if they are both moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation:
Let the length of train B be 2X meters and the speed of train B be 3Y meters/sec.

Given that the length of train A is half that of train B and the speed of train A is one-third of that of train B.

⇒ The length of train A = 2X/2 = X meters.

⇒ The speed of train A = 3Y/3 = Y meters.

Formula:

Time = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Relative speed = difference of their speeds (if they go in the same direction)

Concept:

When train A crosses a man, the relative speed of train A with respect to the man is the speed of train A minus speed of man (=0 as he is at rest) which is the same as the speed of train A.

Calculation:

Time taken by train A to cross the man is given as 48 seconds.

Time = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Time taken to cross the man = Length of train A / Speed of train A

 ⇒ 48 = Length of train A / Y

Length of train A = 48Y

Also, we know that the length of train A is X meters, so we can write:

⇒ 48Y = X

⇒ Y = X/48

Now, we can calculate the time taken by train B to cross train A using the formula:

Time taken by train B = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Total distance to be covered = Length of train A + Length of train B

Total distance to be covered = X + 2X = 3X

Relative speed of train B with respect to train A = Speed of train B - Speed of train A

Relative speed of train B with respect to train A = 3Y - Y = 2Y

Time taken by train B = 3X / 2Y

Substituting Y = X/48,

⇒ Time taken by train B = 3X / 2(X/48) = 72

Time taken by train B = 72 seconds = 60 + 12 = 1 minute 12 secs

Therefore, train B will take 1 minute 12 seconds to cross train A if they go in the same direction. Hence, the answer is 1 minute 12 seconds.

questions.text: A certain sum is deposited at a rate of 40% compounded annually. The difference between interest earned in the 1st year and 2nd year is Rs 384. Find the sum.
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

In compound interest, the difference between the interest of consecutive years is the interest on the interest of the previous year.

Difference = 1st year interest × Rate%

384 = (Principal × 40%) × 40%

384 = P × 0.4 × 0.4 ⇒ 384 = P × 0.16

P = 384 ÷ 0.16 = 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Alternate Method

Given: Rate (R) = 40%, Difference (D) = Rs. 384

Formula: CI for 1st year = P × (R/100); CI for 2nd year = [P + CI1] × (R/100)

⇒ Let Principal be P.

⇒ Interest for 1st year (I1) = P × 40/100 = 0.4P

⇒ Interest for 2nd year (I2) = (P + 0.4P) × 40/100 = 1.4P × 0.4 = 0.56P

⇒ Difference = I2 − I1 = 0.56P − 0.4P = 0.16P

⇒ 0.16P = 384

⇒ P = 384 ÷ 0.16 = 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage for CI

For a rate r%, the effective 2-year CI rate is r + r + (r×r)/100. For 40%, it is 40 + 40 + 16 = 96%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is P(R/100)2. In this question, notice that the 1st year CI is equal to the 1st year SI.

Interest on Interest

Compound interest grows because the interest earned in previous periods itself earns interest at the given rate in subsequent periods.

questions.text: In how many ways a cricket team of 11 cricketers containing 1 wicket keeper, 4 bowlers, 4 batsmen and 2 all rounders can be formed from a group of 24 cricketers containing 2 wicket keepers, 7 bowlers, 6 all rounders and 9 batsmen?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Total ways = 2C1 × 7C4 × 9C4 × 6C2

Total ways = 2 × 35 × 126 × 15

Total ways = 70 × 1890 = 132300

∴ The correct answer is 132300.

Alternate Method

Given:

Wicket Keepers (WK): 2 available, 1 to be selected.

Bowlers (BW): 7 available, 4 to be selected.

Batsmen (BT): 9 available, 4 to be selected.

All Rounders (AR): 6 available, 2 to be selected.

Formula used: nCr = n! / [r! × (n − r)!]

⇒ Ways to select WK = 2C1 = 2! / (1! × 1!) = 2

⇒ Ways to select BW = 7C4 = 7C3 = (7 × 6 × 5) / (3 × 2 × 1) = 35

⇒ Ways to select BT = 9C4 = (9 × 8 × 7 × 6) / (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 126

⇒ Ways to select AR = 6C2 = (6 × 5) / (2 × 1) = 15

⇒ Total ways = 2 × 35 × 126 × 15

⇒ Total ways = 70 × 1890 = 132300

∴ The correct answer is 132300.

Additional Information

Combination Property

The formula nCr = nCn-r is highly useful for simplifying calculations when r is more than half of n.

Fundamental Principle of Counting

If one task can be done in 'm' ways and another in 'n' ways, then both can be done in m × n ways when the tasks are independent.
